---
title: "Session 13 guided lab: loops, apply, and timing"
---

Work in **BIOS6301-mywork.Rproj**. Copy either the [Quarto starter](starter/iteration-lab.qmd)
or [R Markdown starter](starter/iteration-lab.Rmd) into `work/session13/` in your personal repository.
Choose one format. All inputs are synthetic and included. The starter renders as supplied;
complete its TODOs and render again. Submit the source and matching HTML.

## 1. Preallocated loop

Calculate one mean per marker using a preallocated numeric vector and a `for` loop with `seq_along()`. Name the results using the column names of `markers`.

## 2. apply and vectorization

Using `visits`, calculate one mean per participant with `apply()` and with `rowMeans()`. Compare their results using `isTRUE(all.equal(...))`. Explain which `MARGIN` selects rows.

## 3. Lists and typed output

Repeat Part 1 using `lapply()` and `vapply(..., numeric(1))`. Inspect the output types and compare the `vapply()` result with your loop result. Explain why one result is a list and the other is a numeric vector.

## 4. Run one benchmark

Run the supplied timing code. It compares a row loop, `apply()`, and `rowMeans()` after checking agreement and warming up. Report the input dimensions and which method has the smallest median time in your run. Explain why a displayed zero does not mean an operation takes no time. Recommend a method in one sentence.

## Optional: purrr

If purrr is installed, use `purrr::map_dbl(markers, mean)` and compare it with your `vapply()` result. No package installation is required for the core lab.

## Finish

Restart R and render the saved report. Keep the code, requested results, and short explanations visible.
